_meta.notes: All URLs verified against PubMed and institutional sources. Tier A = peer-reviewed original research. Tier B = systematic review/meta-analysis. Tier C = authoritative review/textbook. Tier D = popular science/media.

sources.reliability_notes: High-impact landmark paper. Published in Cell Metabolism (IF ~30). Original mouse and human tissue data.
sources.title: Declining NAD+ Induces a Pseudohypoxic State Disrupting Nuclear-Mitochondrial Communication during Aging
key_claims: NAD+ levels in aged skeletal muscle are approximately 50% of those in young muscle
Declining NAD+ activates HIF-1α leading to pseudohypoxic state
Restoring NAD+ with NMN reverses mitochondrial decline in aged mice

sources.reliability_notes: Randomized controlled study. Clear protocol and outcome data on CoQ10 depletion by statins.
sources.title: Atorvastatin Decreases the Coenzyme Q10 Level in the Blood of Patients at Risk for Cardiovascular Disease and Stroke
key_claims: Atorvastatin 80mg/day for 30 days decreased plasma CoQ10 by 49%
CoQ10 depletion occurred regardless of baseline cardiovascular risk
Effect was dose-dependent

sources.reliability_notes: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Published in BMJ. Well-controlled methodology.
sources.title: Iron supplementation for unexplained fatigue in non-anaemic women: double blind randomised placebo controlled trial
key_claims: Iron supplementation significantly reduced fatigue in women with serum ferritin <50 μg/L but without anemia
p<0.001 for fatigue reduction vs placebo at 12 weeks
Benefit seen even without clinical anemia diagnosis

sources.org: Antioxidants & Redox Signaling / Mary Ann Liebert
sources.reliability_notes: RCT in CFS patients. Sample size moderate (n=73). Published in peer-reviewed journal.
sources.title: Does Oral Coenzyme Q10 Plus NADH Supplementation Improve Fatigue and Biochemical Parameters in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome?
key_claims: CoQ10 200mg + NADH 20mg daily for 8 weeks significantly improved fatigue in CFS patients
Combination reduced fatigue scores vs placebo (p<0.05)
Also improved cognitive function and autonomic function

sources.reliability_notes: Double-blind crossover RCT. Well-designed, published in peer-reviewed phytomedicine journal.
sources.title: Rhodiola rosea in stress induced fatigue — A double blind cross-over study of a standardized extract SHR-5 with a repeated low-dose regimen on the mental performance of healthy physicians during night duty
key_claims: Rhodiola rosea extract SHR-5 at 170mg/day for 2 weeks significantly improved mental performance and reduced fatigue in physicians on night duty
Statistically significant improvement on attention, speed and accuracy of perceptual and cognitive tasks
No significant side effects observed

sources.reliability_notes: RCT in healthy older adults. Rigorous design. Published in high-impact journal.
sources.title: Chronic Nicotinamide Riboside Supplementation Is Well-Tolerated and Elevates NAD+ in Healthy Middle-Aged and Older Adults
key_claims: NR 1000mg/day for 6 weeks increased whole blood NAD+ by approximately 60% in healthy middle-aged and older adults
NR supplementation was safe and well-tolerated
Blood pressure showed a trend toward reduction in subjects with elevated baseline BP

sources.org: Indian Journal of Psychological Medicine / Medknow
sources.reliability_notes: Double-blind RCT. High-concentration full-spectrum ashwagandha root extract (KSM-66). Validated stress/anxiety scales used.
sources.title: A prospective, randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled study of safety and efficacy of a high-concentration full-spectrum extract of Ashwagandha root in reducing stress and anxiety in adults
key_claims: KSM-66 Ashwagandha 300mg twice daily for 60 days significantly reduced serum cortisol by 27.9% vs placebo
Significant improvements in all stress and anxiety scales
Significant improvements in self-reported energy and sleep quality

sources.reliability_notes: High-quality pharmacokinetic study. Demonstrates bioavailability of NR in humans.
sources.title: Nicotinamide riboside is uniquely and orally bioavailable in mice and humans
key_claims: A single oral dose of NR (100-1000mg) was absorbed and elevated blood NAD+ metabolites dose-dependently
NR is uniquely bioavailable compared to other NAD+ precursors
Validated NR as effective oral supplement for raising NAD+

sources.reliability_notes: Review paper by leading mitochondrial psychobiology researcher Martin Picard and Bruce McEwen.
sources.title: Why is Stress Bad for the Brain? A Conceptual Framework for the Role of Mitochondria in Behavioral Epigenetics, Plasticity, and Psychopathology
key_claims: Mitochondria are not just passive energy producers — they actively respond to and signal psychosocial stress
Chronic psychological stress impairs mitochondrial morphology and function
Mitochondrial dysfunction mediates stress-induced brain changes

sources.reliability_notes: Classic paper on tissue CoQ10 levels across age groups. Often cited for age-related CoQ10 decline data.
sources.title: Age-related changes in the lipid compositions of rat and human tissues
key_claims: CoQ10 levels in human heart tissue decline significantly with advancing age
Tissue CoQ10 peaks in early adulthood and declines progressively thereafter
Heart and liver showed most pronounced CoQ10 decline with age

sources.reliability_notes: WHO authoritative fact sheet on global anemia / iron deficiency prevalence.
sources.title: Anaemia — WHO Fact Sheet
key_claims: Anaemia affects approximately 1.92 billion people globally
Iron deficiency is the most common cause of anemia worldwide
Women of reproductive age and children under 5 are most affected
